title: Karam Singh’s Breakthrough and the Durrani Retreat

blocks.text: Karam Singh's reckless bravery becomes the emblem of the Khalsa attack, and even after losing his turban he keeps pressing forward bare-headed into the fight. The Pathans shelter behind the cannons and try to stabilize their line, but the Sikh advance refuses to break.

As the pressure mounts, the Durrani formation begins to collapse and signs of surrender and confusion appear, including white flags raised amid the disorder. Dina Beg sends word praising the Singhs for the victory and asking them to hold their ground rather than scatter into uncontrolled pursuit.

The key instruction is do not pursue the fleeing enemy, because the Nawab wants the field secured before the rout becomes a looting chase. Even so, the page ends with the Khalsa conscious that it has broken the enemy's confidence and forced a major retreat.
